title: The base change of a dominant morphism along an open morphism is dominant
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The claim is that for a dominant f : X -> S and an open g : S' -> S, the base change f' : X times_S S' -> S' is again dominant (statement lines 1336-1338). The proof is a contradiction that has to move between three levels: it assumes f' is not dominant so that its image lies in a proper closed B, passes to the nonempty open U = S' minus B, uses openness of g together with density of f(X) to find x in X with f(x) in g(U), and then changes the base to W = Spec(kappa(f(x))). The step that carries the content is the last one: over the spectrum of a field the two nonempty pullbacks X_W and U_W must have a nonempty fibre product, which yields a point of X times_S S' landing in U and contradicts the containment in B (proof lines 1346-1351). This is H2: the argument is short and uses no hypothesis beyond dominance and openness, but the residue-field base change and the nonemptiness of a fibre product over a field are the non-formal moves, and neither is merely a citation in the author's text.
